key_insight: A high-order FR/CPR solver coupled with a rotating actuator-line model can predict VAWT blade aerodynamics accurately on fixed Cartesian grids without resolving blade geometry.
engineering_relevance: This provides a geometry-free, computationally efficient tool for wind-turbine analysis and parametric design studies, especially for large-scale simulations.
method: Couple FR/CPR flow solver with rotating ALM on a fixed Cartesian mesh
Project blade loads through an isotropic Gaussian kernel in a blade-attached frame
Use a modified dynamic-stall model and DMST correction for coarse-mesh inflow recovery
evidence_signal: The approach was validated against near-wake experiments and prior LES-ALM results, with the mean wake profile matching well and power coefficient within about 6% of high-fidelity LES-ALM near optimal operating conditions.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on choosing a sufficiently resolved Gaussian projection kernel and applying the coarse-mesh induction correction appropriately; otherwise the model may drift into mesh-controlled behavior.
paper_title: A High-Order Flux Reconstruction Actuator-Line Framework for Rotating-Blade Aerodynamics on Fixed Cartesian Grids
